barCharacter: Vera Oberlin. Her comedic job is the closest match: top of the hierarchy, never asks permission, treats everyone as staff ('my most trusted advisor'), and the status move is the joke ('You'd be willing to cover up the literal murder I've committed, no questions asked. notes: Reference file found and read in full (monster-prom-lines.md, plus charm-notes.md). HEAD TO HEAD. Ours, best 12: (1) I wrote a love letter with no ask in it. It looked underdressed. I added a fee. (2) A reply. An actual reply. I am marking it unread so I can open it again. (3) Understood. I shall be in the drafts folder, where I am perfect. (4) Esteemed Motherboard, I have come to formally accept your child's proposal. (5) One: the court adores you. Two: the court has met you. (6) Worst entry? My tax return. Eleven palaces, declared honestly. The tax office marked it as spam. (7) Your own unsubscribe button. Gold-plated. Purely decorative. (8) Subject: my last line. Please disregard. A corrected version follows. It is longer. (9) Bold. Unsolicited. I would know. (10) Sir Quill, I outrank you. Kneel. Slower. Iambically. (11) Maximilian, the palace doorman retires on Friday. I have put your name forward. (12) If {rival} wins, I will be gracious. Then I will annex {rival}. Vera, best 12 (corpus numbers): #4 intro 'a mean, self-made gorgon with a merciless sense of business'; #12 'Sorry, I'm focusing on my career... my career on not dating losers like you!'; #45 'such a chore being this beautiful all the time'; #46 'the superiority of the Cools over the Un-Cools'; #47 'cover up the literal murder I've committed, no questions asked. Right?'; #48 'Right. Now.'; #49 'And since you're SUCH a good advisor...'; #51 the feminism lecture that comes out as an order; #52 'scotch, red wine, the tears of [her] enemies, and straight up poison'; #53 'for some reason it's not a death stare this time'; #54 'attempting to tame her hair with a cattle prod'; #55 'serious situation if it's causing Vera to show empathy'. (a) VOICE: bar. Prince's best lines are identifiable mostly by vocabulary (Subject, unsubscribe, drafts, unread, attachment, Motherboard), which is topic, not shape. Lines 9 to 12 carry no email noun and read as Maximilian. Vera's shape survives without her nouns: complaint as boast (#45), repeat-and-turn fake-out (#12), presumption closed with a two-syllable tag (#47, #48). (b) CONSTRUCTION: ours. Prince's top 12 are tighter than Vera's top 12: every one lands its turn on the last word or two ('fee', 'again', 'perfect', 'spam', 'decorative', 'longer', 'Iambically', 'annex {rival}'), with no wasted clause, while three of Vera's twelve (#46, #49, #50-type prompts) are functional event openers rather than jokes. (c) QUOTABLE: bar, narrowly. Prince's best are smile-and-nod wry; Vera's murder cover-up, 'tears of her enemies' and 'cattle prod' are the ones people clip, because Monster Prom pairs huge stakes with zero sincerity and Prince keeps his stakes administrative. Ours does not match the bar on all three, so the bar wins. Across the whole bank (112 lines), the top 15 to 20 are genuinely good, but 45 lines (40%) are cross-cast, stock, self-explaining, or one of the house templates; the staffing gag alone is 13 lines. Continuity issues: Won {wins} vs Replies received: zero; the accountant replies, yet the first reply in twelve years is the star's no, yet he has 'once received a reply'. Cross-file: Maximilian's bank already owns 'a small country' and 'I own', which is where Prince's voice is leaking.
